title: throughput safety-net and priming scripts
body:
Summary:

This note collects an operational "safety-net" and a set of repeatable priming scripts for throughput benchmarking runs. The goal is to reduce false negatives (runs that look bad due to transient factors) and false positives (observed regressions that are actually noisy artifacts). Focus is throughput harness runs for multi-GPU hosts and quantized model paths.

Why this exists:
- We keep re-running benches because a single noisy run invalidates CI gating.
- Common noise sources: thermal throttling, background maintenance jobs, clock governors, unpredictable RNG entropy, transient network congestion to storage/metric exporters.

When to use:
- Full harness runs (ramp-to-plateau) intended for capacity claims or release notes.
- Validation of model/quantization/encoder changes before shipping a Dedicated capacity update.

High-level approach:
1) Run a lightweight precheck battery that verifies host health and idempotent environment. If any prechecks fail, abort the run (safety-net).
2) Execute a deterministic priming sequence (fixed seed, staged client concurrency) to get devices into steady-state and warm KV cache where applicable.
3) Run the real throughput sweep with consistent telemetry collection.
4) Post-run sanity checks: thermals, GPU clock drift, lost packets, RPC retries.

Safety-net signals (abort if any true):
- GPU thermals: any GPU > 85C during precheck or ramp.
- GPU clocks: sustained clock drop > 200 MHz during ramp.
- Background CPU steal: > 5% steal across 60s window on any host.
- NVLink/IB errors: link error counters increased between precheck and start.
- Disk IO spikes: iowait > 10% continuous for 30s.
- Exporter lag: metrics flush > 120s or out-of-order telemetry.
- Host maintenance windows scheduled within next 24 hours (check metadata).

Precheck script (order matters):
- Lock instance to bench mode: disable cron, kill non-essential user processes (defined whitelist), set CPU governor to performance, set NV power profile to max_perf.
- Clear caches that could cause variance: echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches (documented, use with caution).
- Verify NVIDIA persistence mode and driver health (nvidia-smi -q).
- Record baseline clocks, temps, and ECC counters.
- Confirm synchronized NTP and monotonic clock drift < 5ms over 5 min.

Deterministic priming sequence (30–180s depending on model):
- Phase 0: small-batch single-token runs from fixed seed, 10 threads, 30s. Purpose: warm kernel caches and trace JIT code paths.
- Phase 1: ramped fan-in: increase concurrency in steps (1, 4, 8, 16) holding each for 15s. Use the same prompt set and RNG seed. Purpose: surface transient contention.
- Phase 2: KV/prefix warm: run representative longer-context requests to ensure KV caches populate and tokenizer caches settle. 45s.
- Phase 3: plateau probe: hold target concurrency for 60s and verify latency/throughput stabilize within 5% window. If not stable, extend probe or abort.

Priming knobs (config):
- seed: 42 (always set unless testing RNG effects)
- client_profile: staircase
- step_duration_s: 15
- plateau_duration_s: 60
- token_budget: 512 (truncate longer requests to this during priming)

Example loadgen snippet (JSON-friendly, paste into harness config):
{
  "seed": 42,
  "profile": "staircase",
  "stages": [
    {"concurrency": 1, "duration_s": 15},
    {"concurrency": 4, "duration_s": 15},
    {"concurrency": 8, "duration_s": 15},
    {"concurrency": 16, "duration_s": 60}
  ],
  "truncate_tokens": 512
}

Repeatability knobs (must be present in bench harness):
- deterministic_seed: exposed and logged at run start and end.
- rng_entropy_sources: disable background sources (e.g., systemd-random-seed) if reproducing microbenchmarks.
- client_time_deltas: fixed simulated arrival jitter distribution with explicit seed.
- hardware_profile_hash: record GPU model, driver, BIOS, microcode, NVLink firmware.

Telemetry to capture (always):
- per-GPU: util, mem_util, SM clock, memory clock, power, temp, ECC counters, PCIe errors.
- per-host: CPU steal, cgroups throttling, iowait, interferers list.
- RPC: retries, queue depth, request/response size, serialization times.
- Harness: seed, config hash, git commit of bench-harness, model artifact id, quantization profile id.

Automatic rollback triggers (safety policies applied post-run):
- If throughput < baseline - 6 * stddev over identical previous anchor runs -> mark as suspect and require manual review.
- If tail p95 latency increases > 25% while median < 10% -> flag as possible scheduling jitter, run again with longer plateau.
- If any ECC or PCIe corrected error increments -> fail the run and open infra ticket.

Chaos injections (recommended for robustness testing, separate from capacity claim runs):
- mid-run CPU steal spike: run cpustress on isolated cores for 20s.
- short network egress latency: tc qdisc netem add dev eth0 delay 30ms 10ms distribution normal for 45s.
- GPU clock throttling emulation: use nvidia-smi to reduce persistent clock by 200 MHz for 60s (requires test-scoped NV policy).
Note: These make the run intentionally noisy; do not use for production throughput claims.

Observability checks after run (quick script):
- compare start/end GPU clocks and temps; diff should be small and monotonic (no sudden drops).
- calculate throughput windows and sliding-window stdev; if > 8% during plateau, mark for rerun.
- verify exporter integrity: all expected series present and no gaps > 30s.

Run checklist (pre-launch):
- [ ] confirm host not in scheduled maintenance
- [ ] run precheck battery (exit code 0)
- [ ] lock bench harness revision and model artifact id
- [ ] set seed and attach to run metadata
- [ ] start continuous trace collection (perf/etrace) if requested
- [ ] execute deterministic priming sequence
- [ ] begin throughput sweep with telemetry tagging

Troubleshooting common artifacts:
- Symptom: sudden throughput drop mid-plateau + power limit hit.
  Action: inspect power capping logs, check DC rails, re-run with power headroom.
- Symptom: plateau not stabilizing, p95 oscillates.
  Action: extend plateau, increase priming duration, verify no background cron jobs.
- Symptom: inconsistent results across runs on identical configs.
  Action: ensure seeds set, capture kernel message buffer (dmesg), compare hardware_profile_hash.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we add thermal soak baseline step where fans are driven to a target RPM before the run? Pros: removes fan hysteresis; cons: additional infra permissions.
- Investigate adding a microbenchmark for PCIe link stability that runs before model load to catch flaky links early.
- Validate whether drop_caches affects some quantized kernels adversely; needs controlled A/B tests.

Appendix: quick command snippets
- Lock harness to git commit: git rev-parse --short HEAD > /tmp/bench.commit
- Precheck thermal read: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,clocks.sm --format=csv,noheader,nounits
- Exporter flush health: curl -sS http://localhost:9100/metrics | wc -l

Notes to self (rough):
- We should add an integration in the console that shows "safety-net abort reason" with links to the last 2 run traces.
- Consider a lightweight k8s mutating admission test that prevents bench pods from scheduling on nodes with recent ECC counts.

Changelog:
- 2024-11-03 Marco: initial draft
- 2024-12-05 Aisha: added chaos injection patterns and example loadgen snippet
- 2025-02-07 Riley: added telemetry and rollback trigger thresholds

End of document.
